issues.description: Constructor/API mismatch for the GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit class: the template's class __init__ signature declares a parameter named 'num_qubits' (def __init__(self, num_qubits: int)) while the solution's reference implementation uses a no-argument constructor (def __init__(self)). This difference in the constructor/API surface is likely unintentional and can confuse students who compare the template and solution: students may expect to pass a num_qubits argument when instantiating the template class (or look for handling of that parameter in the template), but the solution demonstrates a different usage. Although not a pure variable-name-only mismatch, it is an identifier/API inconsistency that raises extraneous cognitive load when mapping the problem description (Exercise 1 initialization) to the template and the provided solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the constructor signatures consistent across template and solution. Either remove the unused 'num_qubits' parameter from the template __init__ (preferred if the number of qubits is fixed in the exercise) or add the same parameter to the solution and use it to initialize self.number_of_qubits_query_register. Update any example instantiation in the problem text or README to match the chosen API so students have a single clear constructor to follow.
